text:
Hockey Wilderness made the case this week that it's time to respect Joel Eriksson Ek as a No. 1 center, and the Wild's top line is doing the arguing. After a win over San Jose, Quinn Hughes said of the Kirill Kaprizov, Matt Boldy and Eriksson Ek line, "I just feel like we can tilt the ice when they're out there," per NHL.com's Heather Rule.

The numbers agree. At 5v5 Minnesota gets 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Eriksson Ek on, almost ten points better than without him, and he's on a seven-game point streak with 16 points in 18 games. The remarkable part is that he's been unlucky: six goals on 10.6 expected, which is the kind of gap that usually closes in the shooter's favour. That's a reversal from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had his results running ahead of his chances. Our projection has him at 21 to 36 more goals. If the finishing catches up with the chances, the No. 1 center argument gets a lot easier to make.
headline: Eriksson Ek is tilting the ice
